input.quote: 20.1 Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer, its Affiliates, and their directors, officers, employees, and agents from each third-party claim and resulting damages, settlements, judgments, penalties, costs, and reasonable attorneys' fees arising from an allegation that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate an intellectual property right.
input.rationale: Section 20 meets the preferred position in full. Vendor gives an unqualified IP infringement defence/indemnity to Customer, its Affiliates and their personnel (20.1) plus indemnities for breach of Applicable Law, bodily injury/property damage, unauthorised access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor, and Vendor's gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud (20.2) — matching and slightly exceeding the model language. Customer's reverse indemnity (20.3) is narrow, limited to unmodified Customer-supplied material used as authorised and Customer's own violation of Applicable Law, with carve-outs for Vendor Technology, modification, combination or instructions. Procedure in 20.4 is balanced and customer-favourable (prompt notice, cooperation at the indemnifying party's expense, defence control with the indemnified party, no prejudicial settlement without consent; late notice excuses only to the extent of material prejudice). 20.5 adds the procure/modify-or-replace/terminate-and-refund remedy for infringement claims and bars termination of unaffected Services, and is backed by the termination right in 9.3. Indemnification obligations are also carved out of the liability cap as "Excluded Claims" under 21.3, so the indemnity is not diluted by a super-cap. No redline needed.
